_doc.what: Per-asset parameters for rig_character.py (Stage 3b of the Siegebound art pipeline — the SKELETAL rig/anim tooling, TASK-160). Sibling of pipeline_manifest.json (the static TRELLIS.2 pipeline). Law: CONVENTIONS.md 'Skeletal rig & animation workstream (M7)'.
_doc.why_separate_manifest: The mesh pipeline (pipeline_manifest.json) and the rig pipeline are COMPLEMENTARY but disjoint stages (SM_<CardID> backs the ghost + fallback; SK_<CardID> is the animated runtime). Keeping rig params here avoids perturbing the carefully-authored mesh manifest and keeps the rig tooling self-contained.
_doc.merging: 'defaults' apply to every asset; per-asset keys override (dict values merge one level deep) — identical to pipeline_manifest.json.
_doc.skeleton: The SHARED humanoid skeleton is 'SiegeBiped' (-> UE 'SKEL_SiegeBiped'). Bone NAMES + hierarchy are the retarget contract: every humanoid unit rigged on 'SiegeBiped' gets identical bone names so UE can share/retarget one skeleton + author locomotion once. Bone POSITIONS are computed per-asset in rig_character.py from the MEASURED game-ready mesh (adaptive fit) x the normalized 'proportions' below, so the same skeleton spec fits a 149-tall militiaman and a 208-tall cavalry rider. Non-humanoid assets (e.g. Ogre) may set skeleton:'bespoke' to get their own auto-skeleton later.
_doc.proportions: Normalized humanoid anchors. *_z are fractions of measured mesh HEIGHT (0=feet, 1=head-top). *_x_frac multiply the MEASURED half-width at that region (shoulder_half / hip_half) so limb roots sit inside the silhouette. foot_forward_frac is a fraction of height (foot points -Y = front). A-pose arms (nearly straight down) maximize skin quality for TRELLIS meshes whose arms rest at the sides.
_doc.proportions_override: PER-ASSET ESCAPE HATCH (TASK-372). An asset entry may carry its own 'proportions' dict; rig_character.py overlays it onto a COPY of the chosen skeleton's proportions (unknown keys hard-fail with exit 2), so the shared spec is never mutated and every asset WITHOUT an override rigs byte-identically. WHEN TO USE IT: the anchors are fractions of the MEASURED BBOX height, so when a mesh's bbox overshoots its BODY height (antlers, a tall crown, a raised banner, a staff above the skull) the SAME fraction resolves to a LARGER absolute height - every anchor lands too HIGH on the body and the whole rig slides UP. MIND THE SIGN, IT IS UP: measured on the Sorcerer, neck_top_z 0.865 landed at 0.9121 of TRUE body height instead of 0.865, and head_top_z 1.0 landed on the ANTLER TIPS instead of the skull. (An earlier TASK-369 board note said an overshooting prop 'slides the rig down the body' - that is BACKWARDS; correcting from the wrong direction would DOUBLE the error instead of removing it.) Fix = measure the INFLATION FACTOR (bbox height / true body height) on the CONFORMED mesh and divide every height-normalized fraction by it: corrected = nominal / factor. Divide the *_z keys AND foot_forward_frac (also height-normalized); do NOT divide the *_x_frac keys - they scale measured HALF-WIDTHS, which an overshooting crown does not inflate. Measure the factor on the mesh, never from the concept (TASK-369's concept-stage guess for the Sorcerer was ~1.09 vs the mesh's true 1.0545 - using it would have over-corrected and slid the rig the other way). Precedent for a per-asset deviation from the shared spec: the 'bespoke' skeleton option above. NOT a place to eyeball-tune a rig you simply dislike - the value must come from a measurement, and the derivation belongs in the asset's _note.
_doc.skinning: 'auto_then_envelope' = try Blender bone-heat automatic weights first; if it errors or leaves > unweighted_fallback_fraction of verts empty, fall back to deterministic segment-distance envelope weighting (never fails, generalizes to the batch). Recorded in rig_report.json.
_doc.anims: Frame LENGTHS at 'fps'. Required actions Idle/Walk/Attack/Death (CONVENTIONS). 'weapon_side' picks which arm drives Attack (r bones sit at -X = the character's right, matching the Footman spear at -X). 'attack_style' selects the Attack pose set in rig_character.py (thrust|swing|overhead|cast|mine).
_doc.outputs: rig_character.py writes the rigged mesh FBX to Content/RawAssets/Characters/<CardID>.fbx and one anim FBX per action to Content/RawAssets/Characters/Anims/<CardID>_<Action>.fbx (raw-asset rule). Previews (turntable + per-anim mp4 + bind stills + contact sheets) + rig_report.json go to Cache/<CardID>/rig/. The AM_<CardID>_Attack MONTAGE is authored in-editor at TASK-162 from A_<CardID>_Attack (a montage wraps a sequence — not a Blender export).

SiegeBiped._desc: 21-bone humanoid: root(non-deform) + pelvis + spine_01/02/03 + neck_01 + head + [clavicle/upperarm/lowerarm/hand]_l|r + [thigh/calf/foot]_l|r. UE-mannequin-style names for future Manny retarget potential. _l bones sit at +X (character's LEFT), _r at -X (character's RIGHT — the -X weapon side).

Rigged on the SHARED SiegeBiped (Footman_Rig root) like every humanoid; the adaptive height/half-width fit absorbs the outstretched fireball arm + held staff (TASK-301: bounds [129.88,99.25,181.94] UE, Z height-fit to 182 = 1.82 m; footprint deeper than a stock humanoid per the Cavalry/Ogre weapon-overhang note). 'cast' (script else-branch = raise-arm-then-drive-forward) reads as a spellcast/HURL, deliberately NOT 'thrust' (the Archer/Longbowman bow-draw read the spec bars). weapon_side 'r' drives the STAFF arm (staff in the right hand; fireball cradled in the left palm per TASK-301) up-and-forward = iconic staff-cast silhouette at RTS camera. Sorcerer._note: TASK-372 AG-A5. GDD/plan: Support unit, ancient-ground consecration, NO ATTACK (the Cleric precedent). Rigged on the SHARED SiegeBiped like every humanoid - armature object stays the constant Footman_Rig root, bone names/hierarchy untouched, so SK_Sorcerer binds to the ONE shared /Game/Characters/SK_Footman_Skeleton. weapon_side 'r' drives the arm at the planted rune-monolith (-X); 'cast' (script else-branch = raise-arm-then-drive-forward) is the consecration gesture read, deliberately NOT 'thrust'. ATTACK CLIP IS PRODUCED ANYWAY - Cleric precedent: one run authors all four actions for free, ASummonedUnit::CacheActionAnimations composes A_Sorcerer_Attack by path, and it becomes the ready-made hook for a ground-consecration gesture. 'Attack' is a SLOT NAME, not a semantic claim that this unit attacks. NO ABP_Sorcerer - the runtime falls back to ABP_Footman. || PROPORTIONS OVERRIDE - THE ANTLER INFLATION CORRECTION (Jonathan's 2026-08-01 ruling: KEEP THE ANTLERS, compensate in the rig; per-asset deviation precedent = the 'bespoke' skeleton option). The antler crown rises ABOVE the skull, so the mesh bbox is TALLER than the body and every fraction-of-height anchor would land too low. MEASURED ON THE CONFORMED MESH (TASK-370 handoff section 6, colour segmentation of pale-green skull vs tan antler on the self-calibrating ortho previews; front/back agree to 0.3%): total bbox height 181.805 UE, skull dome apex 172.42 UE => TRUE BODY HEIGHT 172.42 UE, antler overshoot 9.39 UE = 5.45% of body, INFLATION FACTOR = 1.0545. Every value above is nominal / 1.0545 (e.g. neck_top_z 0.865 -> 0.82029; head_top_z 1.0 -> 0.94832 = the skull apex, NOT the antler tips). Each corrected fraction resolves to within 0.01 UE of nominal x 172.42, which is the whole point. DO NOT 'FIX' THESE BACK and DO NOT re-derive: TASK-369's CONCEPT-STAGE ~9.2% estimate (which predicted neck_top_z ~0.94) is SUPERSEDED - Meshy pulled the tines more outward and less vertical than the 2D concept implied, and dividing by ~1.09 would over-correct and slide the rig the other way. Two measurement methods were tried and REJECTED as unsound: vertex Z-slice clustering (sampling noise at 7,496 verts, gave 21.78%) and silhouette width (fooled by converging tines, gave 7.76%). head_base_z is included because build_armature's old bare 0.905 literal is now a proportions key - without it the head bone would stay stranded at the antler-inflated height while every other anchor moved. foot_forward_frac is included because it too is a fraction of HEIGHT (magnitude: 20.00 -> 18.96 UE of toe offset). The *_x_frac keys are deliberately NOT overridden - they scale measured HALF-WIDTHS, which antlers do not inflate. Two-slot [TeamRegion, SorcererPBR]+UVMap from SM_Sorcerer (15,000 tris, feet-center).
